title: Fractional Release Orchestrator: drift-aware slow-roll with staged feature-flag gates
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: Our current progressive delivery primitives (percent ramps, canaries, and feature flags) are fragmented across services and don't account for model drift or correlated regressions during long slow-rolls. Engineers are manually tuning hold-windows and rollback thresholds which leads to inconsistent safety behavior between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.

Goal: Build a Fractional Release Orchestrator (FRO) that coordinates percent traffic ramps, feature-flag gates, and auto-rollback policies while being drift-aware (quality regressions over time) and LTS-aware (different gating for LTS channels). The FRO should: 1) define reusable policies, 2) run deterministic percent ramps with hold windows, 3) detect gradual regressions using sliding windows, 4) integrate with the feature-flag service and console for manual overrides, and 5) expose telemetry and simulation tooling for preflight validation.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Implement a declarative policy DSL that can express: percent ramp schedule, per-metric thresholds, sliding-window drift rules, and feature-flag bindings. 2) New orchestration service executes a sample slow-roll plan across a test cluster that follows the configured schedule and enforces auto-rollback when thresholds are exceeded. 3) Console shows a per-cohort dashboard (error rate, P99, model-quality delta, request volume). 4) Simulated kernel on CI can run a rollout plan and produce deterministic signal traces for verification. 5) Documentation and runbook published: how to author policies for LTS vs non-LTS, and how to trigger manual override/abort.
rollout_plan:
Stage: Shadow -> Canary -> Fractional Ramp -> Global.
Schedule (example): 0% shadow for 24h, 0.1% canary for 1h, hold 30m, 1% for 1h, hold 1h, 5% for 2h, hold 2h, 20% for 4h, hold 4h, 50% then 100%.
Hold windows are configurable per-policy.
Auto-rollback rules: roll back immediately if: (1) 5xx rate increases by >200% over baseline in a 5m sliding window; (2) P99 latency regresses by >2x sustained for >15m; (3) model-quality metric (from eval hooks) drops by >=6% absolute in a 1h window.
Drift detection: sliding-window linear trend test on quality metric with configurable sensitivity; only enforced after minimum incidence (e.g., >=1000 requests in window) to avoid false positives.
Feature-flag binding: each policy can attach to a flag key and will only allow ramping if flag is ON and not revoked by admin.
LTS differences: LTS channels default to slower ramps (max step 10x longer per stage) and stricter thresholds by default.
simulation_results: Local CI simulation running workload profile 'chat-bursty-large-context' executed three predefined rollout plans. Results: safe plan (our recommended defaults) produced no auto-rollbacks and stable metrics across the 0->100 ramp. Aggressive plan triggered two auto-rollbacks at 5% and 20% due to elevated P99 and quality drift. Simulation artifacts uploaded to GCS for review. See PR notes for logs/plots.
risks_mitigation:
Risk: False positives causing unnecessary rollbacks for small noisy workloads. Mitigation: require minimum sample sizes and use both latency+error+quality signals; add a 'cooldown' after transient spikes.
Risk: Console/operator confusion with too many policy fields. Mitigation: ship with opinionated defaults and a simple 'guided' policy template for common cases.
Risk: Cross-region and Dedicated customers with restricted routing. Mitigation: FRO will support region-scoped plans and allow per-deployment overrides; document limitations in Private deployments.

next_steps: 1) Merge prototype API (PR #486) and deploy to staging. 2) Run extended simulations with workload variants (low-volume, bursty, multi-tenant) to tune thresholds. 3) Implement feature-flag integration and console hooks for manual override/abort. 4) Schedule an ops runbook review and tabletop exercise with SRE and Solutions Engineering.
notes: This ticket focuses on orchestration and safety policy expressiveness. Separate follow-ups will handle autoscaling interaction, cost-aware routing, and RBAC for policy editing. Consider combining with ENG-712400 (policy auditing) in a later cycle.
estimated_impact: Improves rollout safety and reduces manual intervention for progressive delivery across Hosted/Dedicated/Private deployments. Expected to reduce rollback toil by ~40% for standard releases based on simulation extrapolation.
